title: Graded traffic attenuation for live-stream cohesion and graceful regional shift
creator: Arianna Chen
description:
Background: Our hosted API gateways operate active-active across regions. Previous tickets have focused on region failover and session affinity, but we still see two failure modes during regional shifts: 1) streaming sessions (long-lived streaming or websocket-style connections) dropping or seeing visible duplications, and 2) sudden global traffic shifts causing transient overload in the chosen target region and triggering cascade circuit-breakers.

Goal: Implement a graded traffic attenuation strategy that preserves live-stream cohesion (no mid-shift stream duplication or inconsistent KV cache state) while preventing overload via progressive traffic drainage and conservative circuit-breaker thresholds. This is NOT a simple all-or-nothing failover. Instead we will: (a) coordinate connection draining for streaming sessions, (b) perform traffic ramps with dynamic shedding priorities, and (c) expose SLO-aware rollback and emergency-cut policies so customer-facing SLAs remain intact.

Scope: The work covers the gateway control-plane changes (traffic steering policies and new traffic-attenuation state machine), runtime helpers for stream reattachment metadata (we will add a short-lived reattach token and stream checkpoints in KV cache), and observability (dashboards/alerts tied to SLO & error-budget consumption during shifts). We will not change client SDKs this cycle; behavior will rely on opaque reattach tokens that existing streaming clients will forward automatically (server-side only).

Non-goals: Building full cross-region synchronized KV (that remains a future project). This ticket focuses on minimizing user-visible disruption without requiring synchronous state replication.
tasks: Design attenuation state machine and APIs for gateway (states: PREPARE, RAMP_UP, PAUSE, RAMP_DOWN, COMMIT, ABORT)
Add reattach token generation and short-lived checkpoint metadata in regional KV cache
Implement per-tenant priority classes for load-shedding (system-critical, billing-critical, interactive-low-latency)
Introduce a soft-throttle that ramps traffic in fractional steps with wait windows and health probes
Define circuit-breaker thresholds during ramp windows and a fast-rollover abort path to source region
Add integration tests for streaming handover and stateless reconnects (simulate spikes and packet loss)
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules (SLO burn rate, target-region queue depth, stream-reconnect-rate)
Perform staged canary across a small tenant set and run chaos scenarios (regional network partition)
acceptance_criteria: Able to shift traffic from region A to region B without dropping >0.1% of active streaming sessions for canary tenants
Target region CPU and scheduler queue depth remain below configured thresholds during ramp (default 70% CPU, queue depth rps threshold)
Circuit-breaker engages and automatically aborts commit path if error-budget burn > 3x over 10m during ramp
SLO-linked alerts (availability p99/time-window) fire and automated rollback completes within configured timeout
No data loss for message checkpoint metadata stored in regional KV for the short-lived reattach window (write ack verified)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit and integration tests in CI; reviewers: runtime and gateway owners
Stage 1: Internal canary (10 internal tenants) with traffic-attenuation enabled; monitoring for 48h
Stage 2: External canary (3% traffic for non-critical tenants) across two regions; watch metrics for 72h
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% with automated rollback capability and on-call engineering present
Stage 4: Full-environment enablement after 14 days of stable behavior and resolved action items
metrics_and_telemetry: SLOs monitored: availability (99.95% monthly), stream-continuity (>=99.9% canary), latency SLO p95 < 250ms for 1k token responses
New metrics: attenuation_state, ramp_fraction, reattach_success_rate, stream_duplication_count, region_queue_depth, cb_open_count
Alerts: reattach_success_rate < 99% (P0), ramp_fraction stalls > 10m (P1), cb_open_count spike (P0)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Target region overload during ramp -> Mitigation: conservative initial ramps (1% increments), health probe gating, per-tenant caps
Risk: Streaming duplication due to clients reconnecting to both regions -> Mitigation: short-lived reattach token with idempotency and checkpoint verification
Risk: Incorrect shedding order causing high-value customers to be shed -> Mitigation: enforce tenant priority classes and run a QA sweep against billing tenants
Risk: False positives in circuit-breaker due to noisy sensors -> Mitigation: use multi-window aggregation and guardrail thresholds before full abort
discussion: 2025-03-13 Miguel Torres: Proposed state machine CR posted as PR #1284. Need runtime review for checkpoint window sizing.
2025-03-14 Ops: We saw during the 2025-02 incident that immediate reroute saturated GPU scheduler — recommend default ramp floor at 0.5% per second and maximum parallel reconnects per node.
2025-03-16 Design (R. Patel): UX for Console rollout step will show live attenuation fraction and allow immediate ABORT; adding mockups to Confluence.
2025-03-18 SRE (L. Nguyen): Added runbook hooks for automatic rollback when SLO burn rate > 5x over 5m. Need SIGINT-safe abort path to avoid double-commits.
notes: Implementation should aim to be backward-compatible with current streaming clients — reattach token is server-generated and opaque
We will store only minimal checkpoint metadata and a short TTL (default 5 minutes) to avoid long-lived cross-region state
If a tenant opts out of graceful drift (explicit setting), we will fall back to immediate failover with higher risk disclosures
